inspiration: Faction read from colour family plus a size tier: one small badge set and one larger set for boss-type mobs, so the faction and the threat level both read at a glance on a radar.

Layered vector maps: each map layer is drawn as thin coloured line strokes with a named colour per layer. A simple layer-colour legend lets a player read terrain, walls and paths without any filled art.
Ground-target marker: a single 64x64 ring with a clear centre, used for ground-targeted area effects. Simple shape language that scales well.
Small bitmap fonts in two sizes for chat and labels: crisp at phone size and cheap to draw in a HUD.
Region table with flag columns (housing, tutorial, instance, water): one row per region with boolean-style flags. Good model for our own zone metadata.
Realm and mob naming lets the art pipeline generate a whole colour family from one base icon.
Zone blurbs are short, one per region, and tied to level bands. Structure is worth copying; the prose is not.

briefs.label: Faction-tier radar badge
briefs.why: A compact badge that reads faction by colour family and threat by size, so a radar full of dots stays legible.
change: use our own faction palette, plus a shape code so colourblind players can tell factions apart
rank shown as a ring count, not a colour variant
distinct glyph per role rather than per colour

briefs.label: Layered line-map style
briefs.why: Thin coloured strokes per layer on a dark ground read like a field map and stay light on the GPU.
keep: fixed legend with one colour per layer
change: tie layers to our biome types, not line colours
draw walls as hatched shapes instead of plain lines
add elevation shading as a second pass

briefs.label: Ground-target ring

change: add a slow pulse or dashed segments
